**Finding: Compliant — no redline proposed.**

The Master Services Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation running in either direction:

- **No MFN language anywhere.** Searches for "most favored nation", "favorable", "no less favorable", "best price", and third-party term-matching patterns all returned zero hits across the document.
- **§5 Fees and Payment (p0023)** is the only commercial-terms provision. It is a plain revenue-share deferred to individual Exhibits, with no benchmarking, rate-card, or price-matching mechanic that could operate as an MFN against AP.
- **§1 (p0001)** actively helps us: the arrangement is expressly non-exclusive and "will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties" — so AP has no obligation to extend Kubient any terms it grants elsewhere.

This satisfies the preferred playbook position (no MFN burden on Customer), so per the rule's direction guidance there is nothing to delete or amend.

One forward-looking watch item: because all pricing and revenue-share terms are pushed into Exhibits, MFN language could surface there. Worth re-running this check when any Exhibit is negotiated or amended.
